The function $f(x)$ is defined and differentiable on the interval $[-5,3].$ The graph of $y={f}^{′}(x),$ the derivative of $f(x),$ is shown above. It consists of three line segments. If $f(3)=13,$ calculate $f(-5).$

$f(-5)=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
From the fundamental theorem of calculus, we find that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-5}^{3}{f}^{′}(x)\,\text{d}x & =f(3)-f(-5) \\ {\int }_{-5}^{3}{f}^{′}(x)\,\text{d}x & =13-f(-5) \\ f(-5) & =13-{\int }_{-5}^{3}{f}^{′}(x)\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Remember that the integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis.

The graph consists of $2$ parts on $[-5,3]:$ the line segment for $x\in [-5,-3]$ and the three line segments for $x\in [-3,3].$ Therefore, we can write the integral as follows:

$$
{\int }_{-5}^{3}{f}^{′}(x)\,\text{d}x={{{\int }_{-5}^{-3}{f}^{′}(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{-{A}_{1}}+{{{\int }_{-3}^{3}{f}^{′}(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{-{A}_{2}}
$$

The first integral ${A}_{1}$ represents the signed area between the line segment and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [-5,-3].$ The corresponding region is a trapezoid, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1} & =\frac{1}{2}(a+b)h \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(1+3)\cdot 2 \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

However, since the region lies below the $x$-axis, we take the area as negative:

$$
{\int }_{-5}^{-3}{f}^{′}(x)\,\text{d}x=-{A}_{1}=-4
$$

The second integral ${A}_{2}$ represents the signed area between the three line segments and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [-3,3].$ The corresponding region is a trapezoid, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{2} & =\frac{1}{2}(a+b)h \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(6+4)\cdot 3 \\  & =15.\end{aligned}
$$

However, since the region lies below the $x$-axis, we take the area as negative:

$$
{\int }_{-3}^{3}{f}^{′}(x)\,\text{d}x=-{A}_{2}=-15
$$

Therefore, the value of the integral is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-5}^{3}{f}^{′}(x)\,\text{d}x & =-{A}_{1}-{A}_{2} \\  & =-4-15 \\  & =-19.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, using the value of the integral, we can find $f(-5):$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(-5) & =13-{\int }_{-5}^{3}{f}^{′}(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =13-(-19) \\  & =32\end{aligned}
$$
